faqs.a: The most common legal limit is 0.08% in many countries, 0.05% or 0.03% in others, and zero for new drivers. Limits vary by country and state, so check your local law and never drive after drinking.
faqs.q: What is the legal alcohol limit for driving?

faqs.a: Widmark's formula is a rough estimate. Your real BAC depends on food, hydration, health, medication and individual metabolism. A breathalyzer or blood test is the only real measurement.
faqs.q: How accurate is the Widmark formula?

faqs.a: One standard drink is about 14 grams of pure alcohol: one 330 ml beer at 5%, one 140 ml glass of wine at 12%, or one 40 ml shot of spirits at 40%. Strong cocktails can equal two or more standard drinks.
faqs.q: What counts as one standard drink?

faqs.a: Nothing speeds up alcohol metabolism. Coffee, cold air and cold showers only wake you up; the alcohol leaves your blood at about 0.015% per hour no matter what you do.
faqs.q: Does coffee sober you up faster?

faqs.a: Women typically have a higher proportion of body fat and less body water than men of the same weight, so the same amount of alcohol produces a higher BAC. The formula uses 0.66 for women and 0.73 for men.
faqs.q: Why do women get a higher BAC from the same drinks?

faqs.a: Eating slows alcohol absorption, so your BAC peaks lower and later than on an empty stomach. But the total alcohol is the same, so it does not make driving safe.
faqs.q: Does eating before drinking lower my BAC?

bac-calculator.formula:
BAC% = (alcohol in oz x 5.14) / (weight in lb x r) - 0.015 x hours
r = 0.73 (male) or 0.66 (female). One standard drink = 0.6 oz of pure alcohol.
The body clears roughly 0.015% per hour.
howTo: Select Male or Female and choose metric (kg) or imperial (lb) units.
Count your standard drinks: 330 ml beer, 140 ml wine or 40 ml spirits each count as one.
Enter the hours since your first drink.
Read your estimated BAC and the approximate hours until it reaches zero.
keyFacts: BAC (blood alcohol concentration) is measured as grams of alcohol per 100 ml of blood, shown as a percentage.
Widmark's 1932 formula is the classic estimate: alcohol divided by body water, minus 0.015% per hour of metabolism.
Men use a distribution factor of 0.73, women 0.66, because women average less body water per kilogram.
A 180-lb man who has 4 standard drinks over 2 hours reaches about 0.064%.
Food slows absorption but does not reduce the total alcohol that must be metabolized.
Only time lowers BAC. Coffee, food and cold air do not speed up alcohol elimination.

bac-calculator.quickAnswer: Widmark's formula estimates blood alcohol from your weight, the number of standard drinks and the hours since your first drink. A 180-lb man who has 4 drinks over 2 hours reaches about 0.064% BAC and needs roughly 4 more hours to reach zero. This is an educational estimate, not legal proof, and you should never drive after drinking.
bac-calculator.tagline: Estimate your blood alcohol level with the Widmark formula - educational estimate, never a reason to drive.
bac-calculator.workedExample:
Male, 180 lb, 4 standard drinks over 2 hours:
1. Alcohol = 4 x 0.6 = 2.4 oz.
2. 2.4 x 5.14 = 12.336; weight factor = 180 x 0.73 = 131.4.
3. 12.336 / 131.4 = 0.0939.
4. Metabolism: 0.015 x 2 = 0.03.
5. BAC = 0.0939 - 0.03 = 0.0639%, about 0.064%.
Time to zero: 0.064 / 0.015 = about 4.3 hours from the estimate.
